# real-chart-bench

> An open benchmark for chart-data-extraction accuracy, built from real experimental
> figures in open-access research papers (not synthetic charts). Ground truth comes from
> Starrydata's human-digitized XY curves (CC BY 4.0), paired with real figure images from
> CC BY 4.0 papers. Evaluates LLMs, dedicated models (e.g. LineFormer), and classic CV
> tools against a common, growing set of manually numeric-cross-verified real charts.
> Pre-alpha: dataset, evaluation harness, and leaderboard are live; the verified
> real-image set is still small and growing (reliability over quantity is a deliberate
> project policy, not a temporary gap).

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): quick start, how to evaluate your own model, how scores are
  computed, how to add results to the leaderboard, data layout, license.
- Live leaderboard: https://t29mato.github.io/real-chart-bench/
- [docs/design/benchmark-architecture.md](docs/design/benchmark-architecture.md): the
  full design history — every architectural decision, every empirical finding from real
  data (license yield rates, panel-splitting failure modes, image-orientation bugs,
  metric design rationale), in dated, numbered sections (§1-§7.49+). This is the
  authoritative source if README's summary isn't enough detail.
- [docs/design/pairing-automation.md](docs/design/pairing-automation.md): the design for
  automating image↔ground-truth pairing — the project's one genuine bottleneck. Candidate
  generation as a per-paper assignment problem, the numeric cross-verification checks and
  their empirically-measured tolerances, confidence thresholds and why the operating point
  is asymmetric, and what is deliberately left un-automated.
- [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff): how to cite this benchmark, and the Starrydata dataset +
  paper you should cite alongside it if you use the ground-truth data.

## Core interfaces (read these before writing code against this repo)

- [src/real_chart_bench/usecase/model_runner.py](src/real_chart_bench/usecase/model_runner.py):
  `ModelRunnerPort` — the one interface you implement to plug a model into the harness.
- [src/real_chart_bench/domain/metrics.py](src/real_chart_bench/domain/metrics.py),
  [matching.py](src/real_chart_bench/domain/matching.py),
  [evaluation.py](src/real_chart_bench/domain/evaluation.py): the scoring logic (pure,
  no I/O, 100% test coverage — read the tests for exact boundary-case behavior).
- [scripts/eval/run_baselines.py](scripts/eval/run_baselines.py): a complete, working
  example wiring a `ModelRunnerPort` into the harness and writing a leaderboard-ready
  results file.

## Data

- [data/manifest/v0/](data/manifest/v0/): committed ground-truth manifest (papers,
  figures, curves), CC BY 4.0.
- [data/verified_pairs/registry.json](data/verified_pairs/registry.json): committed
  audit trail of manually verified (and rejected) image↔ground-truth pairings, with
  numeric evidence and a `license_id` on every entry. Rejected entries additionally carry
  a `rejection_category` (`pairing` / `image` / `gt_suspect`) separating our own errors
  from suspected upstream ground-truth errors; a `gt_suspect` entry carries a
  `gt_suspect_status` lifecycle (`llm_flagged` → `human_confirmed` / `human_rejected`).
  **`llm_flagged` alone is a suspicion, never a confirmed ground-truth error** — only
  `human_confirmed` counts (design §7.48).
- `data/raw/` is gitignored (regeneratable); run
  [scripts/eval/fetch_verified_images.py](scripts/eval/fetch_verified_images.py) to
  fetch just what the verified-pairs registry needs.

## For coding agents modifying this repo

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for setup, test/lint commands, and architecture conventions
(clean architecture with a machine-enforced dependency direction, TDD, 100%
domain-layer coverage requirement).
